title: Five White Kites
checkpoint: Phase 5 (School readiness) — new sound 'i-e' (the split spelling as in kite, five and white)
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the split spelling 'i-e'. Another team with a letter in the middle — k-i-t-e. Your child already knows 'igh' and 'ie' for this same sound, so this is a third way to write it.

pages.text: It was a fine day for kites. Pip had five, and all five of them were white.
pages.illustration: Pip the sparrow on a breezy hilltop holding five kite strings in his beak and both feet, five white diamond kites climbing above him against a huge pale blue sky. Lots of open air.

pages.text: Fig had never seen a kite. He did not like the look of them one bit.
pages.illustration: Fig the caterpillar flat on the grass, gripping a stem with all his legs, staring up at the kites with deep suspicion. Low worm's-eye viewpoint so the kites loom enormous.

pages.text: "They bite," said Fig. Pip said kites do not bite. Fig was not sure.
pages.illustration: Close two-shot: Pip patient and reasonable, Fig unconvinced with his little face set. One kite string coiling near Fig like a snake, which is clearly why he thinks this.

pages.text: The wind got strong. The kites went right up, high and white and small.
pages.illustration: The kites tiny and far off near the top of the page, strings stretched taut and thrumming, grass flattened below. Pip leaning back hard against the pull. Emphasise wind with bent stems.

pages.text: Then one string went snap. The white kite went off past the trees, all by itself.
pages.illustration: A snapped string whipping loose and one kite tumbling away over the treetops, getting smaller. Pip's expression stricken. The other four kites still up. Wide open sky.

pages.text: Olive went after it. Olive is not quick, but she is quick when she is cross.
pages.illustration: Olive the owl in full flight, wings swept back, absolutely determined, moving faster than an owl of her build should. Streaks of movement. Genuinely impressive and slightly frightening.

pages.text: She came back with it. "Nine trees," she said. "It went nine trees."
pages.illustration: Olive landing with the muddy kite held in one foot, entirely unruffled, delivering her report. Pip and Fig looking up at her with enormous respect. Comic understatement.

pages.text: Fig held a string after that. Just the one. He held it as tight as tight.
pages.illustration: Fig on the grass with one kite string wound firmly around his middle three times, one small white kite bobbing above him, a look of intense concentration and secret delight. Final warm evening light.
